title: C4931007 - A Study to Learn About the Safety of an Expanded Pneumococcal Vaccine in Healthy Infants
official: C4931007 - A PHASE 3, RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLIND TRIAL TO EVALUATE THE SAFETY AND TOLERABILITY OF A MULTIVALENT PNEUMOCOCCAL CONJUGATE VACCINE IN HEALTHY INFANTS
summary: Main objective: To describe the safety profile of the PG4 vaccine

interventions.name: Prevenar 20 suspension for injection in pre-filled syringe Pneumococcal polysaccharide conjugate vaccine (20-valent, adsorbed)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Male or female infants 2 months of age (≥42 to ≤98 days) at the time of consent (the day of birth is considered the first day of life).
2. Healthy infants determined by clinical assessment, including medical history and clinical judgment, to be eligible for the study.
3. Participants whose parent(s)/legal guardian is willing and able to comply with all scheduled visits, treatment plan, and other study procedures.
4. Expected to be available for the duration of the study and whose parent(s)/legal guardian can be contacted by telephone during study participation.
5. Participants whose parent(s)/legal guardian is capable of giving signed informed consent as described in Section 10.1.3, which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the ICD and in this protocol.
Exclusion criteria:
1. History of severe adverse reaction associated with a vaccine and/or severe allergic reaction (eg, anaphylaxis) to any component of study intervention or any diphtheria toxoid–containing vaccine.
2. Receipt of treatment with known systemic immunosuppressant medications (including cytotoxic agents, eg, for cancer or an autoimmune disease) from birth or planned receipt through conclusion of the study. Receipt of blood/plasma products or immunoglobulins (including hepatitis B immunoglobulin) since birth or planned receipt through Visit 6. Note: Topical medications with local immunosuppressive effect for management of skin disorders (eg, tacrolimus ointment for atopic dermatitis) are permitted throughout the study. Receipt of systemic corticosteroids ≥2 mg/kg/day of prednisone or equivalent in participants <10 kg, or 20 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent in participants ≥10 kg, for ≥14 days within 28 days before enrollment or planned receipt through conclusion of the study. Note: Inhaled/nebulized, epidural, intra-articular, or topical (skin, eyes, or eyes) corticosteroids are permitted.
3. Investigational drugs, vaccines, or medical devices are prohibited from study entry throughout the course of the study, until study completion at Visit 7.
4. Children, grandchildren, or other individuals who are direct descendants of investigator site staff or sponsor and sponsor delegate employees directly involved in the conduct of the study.
5. Significant neurological disorder or history of seizure, including febrile seizure, or significant stable or evolving disorders such as cerebral palsy, encephalopathy, hydrocephalus, or other significant disorders (including those associated with prematurity, ie, intracranial hemorrhage, apnea requiring supplemental oxygen or home monitor, severe bronchodysplasia, etc). Does not include resolving syndromes due to birth trauma, such as Erb’s palsy and/or hypotonic-hyporesponsive episodes.
6. Major known congenital malformation or serious chronic disorder.
7. History of microbiologically proven invasive disease caused by S. pneumoniae
8. Known or suspected immunodeficiency or other conditions associated with immunosuppression, including, but not limited to, immunoglobulin class/subclass deficiencies, DiGeorge syndrome, generalized malignancy, leukemia, lymphoma, or organ or bone marrow transplant.
9. Bleeding diathesis or condition associated with prolonged bleeding that would, in the opinion of the investigator, contraindicate intramuscular injection.
10. Congenital, functional, or surgical asplenia.
11. Other acute or chronic medical condition or laboratory abnormality that may increase the risk of study participation or study intervention administration or may interfere with the interpretation of study results and, in the investigator’s judgment, make the participant inappropriate for the study.
12. Previous vaccination with any licensed or investigational pneumococcal vaccine, or planned receipt through study participation. Note: Investigational vaccines authorized for temporary or emergency use will be permitted during the course of this study if administered more than 14 days prior to or 14 days after study intervention.
